headline: Host-linked genomic structure across coral, plant, protist, and viral systems
label: Host Associated Genomic Diversity
summary: Recent preprints and a 2026 publication pair genome-scale profiling with host genetics and population sampling across diverse taxa.
synthesis: The common thread is the use of genome-scale profiling to resolve structure within host-associated or environmental systems. In the coral Acropora hemprichii, scRNA-seq with pseudo-aligned transposable element quantification resolves eight cell types and links cell-type-specific TE transcription to symbiosis and calcification programs. A population-scale polyA RNA-seq study shows that leaf transcriptomes yield enough fungal reads to profile phyllosphere mycobiomes and to map host genetic control through GWAS and TWAS. A dual-target AmpSeq panel genotypes both Neoparamoeba perurans and its kinetoplastid symbiont Perkinsela from xenic samples, revealing asymmetric population structure. Paramecium mitochondrial genomes from global samples show cryptic diversity and purifying selection with little recombination. A published study finds that DNA viral genomes from estuaries and globally are niche-partitioned and carry host-like osmoadaptive protein traits.
